summary:
FSD (Supervised) is a subscription in the U.S.: Tesla lists $99 a month and no longer sells it outright [2][3]. New U.S. and Canadian Teslas have come with only Traffic-Aware Cruise Control since January; Autosteer needs FSD. Not a Tesla App reports Musk made that call himself to lift subscriptions, which Tesla hasn't confirmed [39]. Tesla counted 1.74 million active FSD subscriptions at the end of Q3 [4].

The software hasn't changed this week: FSD v14.3.13 on AI4 cars and v14.3 Lite on HW3, in 2026.38.5.12 [1][27]. HW3 still won't get unsupervised FSD, and Tesla's target for unsupervised FSD in owners' cars is Q2 2027, inside Robotaxi zones first [5][6].

Robotaxi grew again. San Antonio launched on November 9 with a 274-square-mile zone on paper, Austin's zone grew to about 443 square miles, and on November 11 Tesla said rides now run around the clock in every city it serves [35][37][38]. Electrek estimates the usable part of each zone is well short of the advertised size [35]. Federal crash reports list 26 Tesla robotaxi incidents in Austin since July 2025 [25].

In Europe, Finland approved the system, sold there as Tesla Assisted Driving, making 11 approvals on the continent; rollout is promised soon [36]. And Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production around mid-2027 to make room for the Cybercab [34].

price.purchase: Can't be bought outright: Tesla says FSD (Supervised) is subscription-only [2]. The $8,000 one-time purchase ended after February 14, 2026 [3].
price.note: FSD bought outright by an earlier owner stays with the car unless it was transferred away before March 31, 2026; a previous owner's subscription does not carry over, and Luxe Package FSD may carry over depending on when it was bought [2].

versions.note: 2026.38.5.11 began rolling October 24 and is the most widely installed build; 2026.38.5.12, with the same FSD, appeared on November 4 [19][27]. Rewritten AI compiler, vision-encoder upgrades and Automatic Collision Evasion [1]. In Europe, AI4 cars run FSD 14.2.2.6 in 2026.39.6, and a 2026.39.100 build with FSD 14.2.2.7 was first seen there on November 10 [27][40]. Tesla's manuals now call this computer SI4 [21].

Distilled from v14 for HW3: parking, unparking, reversing, Arrival Options and Speed Profiles, including a new SLOTH profile; carried in 2026.38.5.11 and the November 4 point release 2026.38.5.12 [1][19][27].

hardware.fsd: None as built: HW2 is not FSD capable [13].
hardware.note: HW2 went into S and X from October 2016 to about August 2017; S/X built earlier in 2016 have the older Autopilot 1 hardware and no FSD path [13].

hardware.fsd: None as built; runs FSD (Supervised) only if the computer was retrofitted to HW3, which Tesla did free for owners who had bought FSD [13].

check: In the car: Controls > Software > Additional Vehicle Information shows the Autopilot computer (2.5, 3 or 4); this needs software 2024.38 or later [12].
Controls > Software also shows whether Full Self-Driving Capability is in the car's included package [2].
Front cameras: AI4 cars show two red lenses and one black dummy lens; AI4 side repeaters have a red tint [12].
Build date: S/X after about March 2023, U.S. Model Y after late May 2023 and the 2024 Model 3 are likely AI4 [12].
Tesla's owner's manuals now call the computer the "SI Computer": HW3 is listed as SI3 and AI4 as SI4. Same hardware, new name [21].
transfer: You can no longer move FSD to another car or account: Tesla's FSD (Supervised) Transfer Program ended on March 31, 2026 [2][3]. If you sell a car whose FSD was bought outright, the purchase stays with that car, so the next owner gets it [2]. If you had a subscription, it ends with your ownership and the buyer must subscribe on their own Tesla account [2]. There is no current transfer offer. The new referral program is not a transfer: subscribers get a free month and outright owners a $99 Tesla credit for each referral who subscribes, up to 12 a year, in app 4.62 or later [30].

robotaxi.status: No one on board; Cybercabs in the fleet [9][14]. On November 9 the zone grew from about 272 to 443 square miles [37]; NHTSA reports list 26 Tesla robotaxi crashes in Austin since July 2025 (25 Model Y, 1 Cybercab) [25]. Texas registrations: 1,080 robotaxis, 573 of them Cybercabs, not all in service [24]
No one on board; Tesla says Cybercab rides start in Dallas this month [6][14][28]
No one on board [14]; on October 26 the zone grew from about 25 to an estimated 254 square miles, by third-party trackers' count [23]
Launched November 2 at 6 a.m.; the zone runs west of downtown to TCU and White Settlement and along I-820 toward Saginaw [28]; reported as unsupervised [33]

Launched November 9 at 5 a.m. with a 274-square-mile zone on paper from Loop 1604 to south of downtown; the airport is inside but not served. Whether rides carry a safety monitor wasn't reported at launch [35]
Safety driver required by California rules; not driverless [5][7]
Announced as coming soon; no dates [7][8]

buying: Check Controls > Software for Full Self-Driving Capability: only an outright purchase stays with the car [2].
Don't count on moving FSD from your old car; transfers ended March 31, 2026 [2].
Prefer AI4: HW3 gets the Lite build and won't run unsupervised FSD [1][5].
On a 2017-2019 S/X or early Model 3, confirm the computer is HW3 or later, not HW2/HW2.5 [12][13].
Budget $99 a month if the car has no purchased FSD [2].
Outside the U.S., don't buy a car with an aftermarket FSD unlock: Korean police booked 80 people for using such devices, which carry up to two years in prison there [26].
Selling a car with purchased FSD? It stays with the car, so price it in; a referral reward is not a way to move it [2][30].
changes: Robotaxi launched in San Antonio on November 9, Tesla's fifth Texas market, with a 274-square-mile zone on paper [35].
Austin's Robotaxi zone grew about 63%, to roughly 443 square miles, on November 9 [37].
On November 11 Tesla said Robotaxi now runs 24 hours a day in every city it serves, up from 5 a.m. to 2 a.m. [38][37].
Finland approved FSD (Supervised), sold in Europe as Tesla Assisted Driving; rollout 'soon', no date [36].
Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production around mid-2027 to build more Cybercabs [34].
Not a Tesla App reports Musk personally cut basic Autopilot (Autosteer) from new U.S. and Canadian cars in January 2026 to push FSD subscriptions; Tesla hasn't confirmed it [39].
No new U.S. FSD release: v14.3.13 and v14.3 Lite in 2026.38.5.12 remain current; Europe saw 2026.39.100 with FSD 14.2.2.7 [27][40].

pt.summary:
O FSD (Supervised) é uma assinatura nos EUA: a Tesla cobra US$ 99 por mês e não vende mais a compra definitiva [2][3]. Desde janeiro, os Tesla novos nos EUA e no Canadá vêm só com o controle de cruzeiro adaptativo; o Autosteer exige FSD. O Not a Tesla App diz que Musk tomou essa decisão pessoalmente para aumentar as assinaturas, o que a Tesla não confirmou [39]. A Tesla contou 1,74 milhão de assinaturas ativas do FSD no fim do 3º trimestre [4].

O software não mudou nesta semana: FSD v14.3.13 nos carros AI4 e v14.3 Lite no HW3, na versão 2026.38.5.12 [1][27]. O HW3 continua sem previsão de FSD sem supervisão, e a meta da Tesla para o FSD sem supervisão nos carros de clientes é o 2º trimestre de 2027, primeiro dentro das zonas do Robotaxi [5][6].

O Robotaxi cresceu de novo. San Antonio estreou em 9 de novembro com uma zona de 274 milhas quadradas no papel, a zona de Austin passou a cerca de 443 milhas quadradas e, em 11 de novembro, a Tesla disse que as corridas agora funcionam 24 horas por dia em todas as cidades atendidas [35][37][38]. A Electrek estima que a área realmente utilizável é bem menor que a anunciada [35]. Relatórios federais listam 26 incidentes com robotáxis da Tesla em Austin desde julho de 2025 [25].

Na Europa, a Finlândia aprovou o sistema, vendido lá como Tesla Assisted Driving, somando 11 aprovações no continente; o lançamento está prometido para breve [36]. E a Tesla vai encerrar a produção da Cybertruck por volta de meados de 2027 para abrir espaço ao Cybercab [34].

de.summary:
FSD (Supervised) ist in den USA ein Abo: Tesla verlangt 99 Dollar im Monat und verkauft es nicht mehr zum Festpreis [2][3]. Neue Teslas in den USA und Kanada haben seit Januar nur noch den Abstandstempomaten; Autosteer gibt es nur mit FSD. Laut Not a Tesla App hat Musk das persönlich entschieden, um die Abozahlen zu steigern; Tesla hat das nicht bestätigt [39]. Ende des dritten Quartals zählte Tesla 1,74 Millionen aktive FSD-Abos [4].

Die Software blieb diese Woche gleich: FSD v14.3.13 auf AI4-Autos und v14.3 Lite auf HW3, in 2026.38.5.12 [1][27]. HW3 bekommt weiterhin kein unbeaufsichtigtes FSD, und Teslas Ziel für unbeaufsichtigtes FSD in Kundenautos ist das zweite Quartal 2027, zuerst in den Robotaxi-Zonen [5][6].

Robotaxi ist erneut gewachsen. San Antonio startete am 9. November mit einer Zone von 274 Quadratmeilen auf dem Papier, Austins Zone wuchs auf rund 443 Quadratmeilen, und am 11. November erklärte Tesla, die Fahrten liefen nun in allen Städten rund um die Uhr [35][37][38]. Electrek schätzt die tatsächlich nutzbare Fläche deutlich kleiner als angegeben [35]. Bundesweite Unfallberichte listen seit Juli 2025 26 Vorfälle mit Tesla-Robotaxis in Austin [25].

In Europa hat Finnland das System zugelassen, dort als Tesla Assisted Driving verkauft – die elfte Zulassung auf dem Kontinent; der Start soll bald folgen [36]. Und Tesla will die Cybertruck-Produktion um Mitte 2027 auslaufen lassen, um Platz für den Cybercab zu schaffen [34].
